Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:82: Likewise they expounded further in Shemot Rabbah (24:1), parashat "And it journeyed" (Exodus 15:22), on the verse (Deuteronomy 32:6), "Is this how you repay the Lord?" etc. — for one of the conditions of being sons is to do their father's will, and then they are called sons and the father does his sons' will, in these words: "is He not your Father who acquired you" — if you have merited it, your Father — just as a son endears himself to his father and the father does his will, so you endear yourselves before Him and He does your will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:83: Another interpretation: if He is your Father, why does it say "who acquired you"? If "who acquired you," why "your Father"? Rather, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, He has mercy on them like a father on his children; and when they do not do His will, He drives them like a servant — just as a servant, whether willingly or unwillingly, must serve his master against his will, so you shall do the will of the Omnipresent, willingly or unwillingly, against your will. Rabbi Tachlifa of Caesarea said in the name of Rabbi Fila: come and see how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performs for a person without his knowing it — for were bread to descend into his innards raw as it is, it would scratch him, but the Holy One, blessed be He, created a spring [saliva/passage] within his gullet that brings the bread down safely. "He made you and established you" — He made you into what you need — and after all this, "is this how you repay the Lord?" — you go and speak superfluous words. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:84: Further, among the things that arouse love, it is explained in Bamidbar Rabbah, parashat Nazir, on the verse (Song of Songs 5:16), "his palate is sweetness, and all of him is delightful," in these words: "all of him is delightful" — Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: it is the way of the world that a laborer works for the householder — because he defiles himself with mud [in the labor], he [the employer] gives him his wage; but the Holy One, blessed be He, warns Israel and says to them: do not defile yourselves with any evil matter, and I will give you your reward. This is what is written (Leviticus 11:43), "do not make yourselves detestable," etc. — what is meant by "I am the Lord"? I am trustworthy to pay a reward for this. Hence, "all of him is delightful."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:85: Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiya said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: it is written (Ezekiel 20:20), "and sanctify My sabbaths" — with what do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. What is written of it? "And they shall be a sign between Me and you, to know that I am the Lord your God" — I am the Lord, trustworthy to pay you reward for this. Hence, "all of him is delightful." "This is my Beloved" — as it says (Leviticus 20:26), "and I have set you apart from the peoples, to be Mine." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:86: Further, among the things that arouse His love for us, blessed be He, is what has been mentioned, that the Shechinah guards us in this exile, as it is written in the Haggadah, "it is this that has stood by our fathers and by us," for not one alone has risen against us, etc., and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand. And our sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma, chapter 7, 69b) that after the Destruction they sought to remove the phrase "the great, the mighty, and the awesome God" [from the Amidah], but the Men of the Great Assembly came and restored it, saying, these very things are His mighty deeds, these are His awesome deeds — that He sustains us among the nations. And they said, great is the Shepherd who guards His flock. And our sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 9a): "His arrows shall consume them" [interpreted as] "His vessels are consumed, but they [Israel] are not consumed" — and this is what the prophet laments (Lamentations 5:22), "unless You have utterly rejected us, and are exceedingly angry with us." The meaning is that if the Holy One, blessed be He, had truly rejected us, His anger would be to the utmost, to consume everything entirely; but since we see that the Holy One, blessed be He, has left us a remnant, His intent in the exile and destruction was only to discipline us so that we return in repentance. Therefore it says, "turn us back to You, O Lord, and we shall return." And so our sages, of blessed memory, said at the end of Megillat Eichah (Eichah Rabbah 5:20), that one who is angry will in the end be appeased, and so it is said through Isaiah (Isaiah 57:16), "for I will not contend forever, nor will I be angry perpetually."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:87: Rabbeinu Bachya, the pious, peace be upon him, wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Contemplation, ch. 5) that the greatest of the good things done for man is the Torah given to us through Moses our prophet, and the showing of signs through him — and if a person in this era wishes to see something resembling those matters, let him look, with the eye of truth, at our standing among the nations from the time of the exile, and the ordering of our affairs among them, etc.; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:88: Besides this, He answers us in all our distresses when we contemplate repentance and regret our sins and undertake fasting and repentance — immediately the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on us; particularly regarding the withholding of rains, this matter has been observed among Israel countless times — for Israel, a holy people, beloved before their Creator, when they decree three fasts, are answered, and thereby the Name of Heaven is sanctified, and it shows that there is a God for Israel — as the prophet said (Jeremiah 14:22), "are there any among the vanities of the nations that can cause rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are You not He, O Lord our God? And we wait for You," etc. This aspect of love thus encompasses all of Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:89: There is another aspect of love, encompassing a portion of the nation of Israel — those who were gathered together after having been scattered, who then returned and took refuge under the wings of the Shechinah — for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, performed countless miracles, and who are thus obligated to give thanks and praise to the Creator, as we say every day, "Blessed is our God who created us for His glory and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us the Torah of truth" — for how many souls were sunk there in the depths of the kelipah, and their departure from there resembles exactly the Exodus from Egypt. Indeed, the essence of our exodus from Egypt was not merely our exodus from physical bondage to redemption, but rather that our souls too were sunk in the kelipah of these idol-worshipers, as it is known from what our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shemot Rabbah 16:2) on "draw out and take" — draw your hands away from idolatry.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:90: Further there is an all-encompassing aspect of love that is also particular to each and every individual according to his rank — when he examines within himself how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, has performed for him from the day he came to awareness, beyond what He did for him in the days of his childhood; and when the Holy One, blessed be He, favors him with wisdom, or wealth, or dominion beyond the rest of the people, he becomes obligated to a particular service to the Creator beyond the general service, more than what the rest of the nation performs. And so Rabbeinu Bachya wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Accepting the Service of God, end of ch. 3), in these words: and when one examines the favors of the Creator upon him, by which He singled out him and his tribe from the rest of the peoples, he should believe himself obligated in the traditional [chok-based] commandments beyond the rest of the nations. And likewise, when he examines God's favor upon him, by which He singled out his tribe and his people from the other tribes of his own people, such as the priesthood and Levitical status, he should believe himself obligated in the commandments by which God singled out his tribe. And therefore you find twenty-four gifts given to the priesthood, corresponding to twenty-four favors the Creator bestowed upon the priests. By this same reasoning, whoever God singles out for a favor beyond other people must obligate himself to a service by which he is distinguished from them, along with his effort in the general service common to all, according to his ability and comprehension — to give thanks to God, blessed be He, for what He singled out for him of good, so that this becomes a cause for its continuation, and He will add to it, to reward his service in the future — and he should not be like those of whom it is said (Hosea 2:10), "and silver I multiplied for her, and gold they made for Baal." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:91: And in chapter 6 he further wrote on this matter: whoever rebels against God with the favor by which He singled him out falls from all the extra ranks, and the Creator is more exacting with his accounting in this world, as it is said (Leviticus 10:3), "this is what the Lord spoke, saying, through those near to Me I will be sanctified," etc., and it says (Amos 3:2), "only you have I known of all the families of the earth, therefore I will punish you," etc.; and his punishment in the World to Come will be even harsher, as it is said (Isaiah 30:33), "for Tophet has been arranged from of old, it too is prepared for the king," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:92: He further wrote: and whatever additional good the Creator grants a person, he is obligated in service for it. And the proof of this is that grain crops are obligated in tithes, as it says, "you shall surely tithe," etc.; and whoever God gave a hundred kors is obligated in ten kors from it, and whoever was given ten kors is obligated in one kor from it; and if the first gives out nine and a half and the second one kor, the first will be punished and the second will receive reward. Likewise, one who has no son is exempted from the obligation of circumcision [for a son] and the study of Torah [with a son]; one who is lame is exempted from the obligation of the pilgrimage festival; one who is ill is exempted from those commandments he cannot perform. By this same reasoning, whoever the Creator, blessed be He, singles out for good is obligated in additional service beyond it. Therefore the early pious ones, when a worldly good came to them, would be fearful of it, for two reasons: first, lest they fall short in completing the service owed for it and giving thanks for it, and it turn to their harm, as our father Jacob, peace be upon him, said (Genesis 32:10), "I am diminished by all the kindnesses," etc.; and second, lest this be [taken as] the Creator's reward for their service [in this world], diminishing their reward in the World to Come, as the early commentators explained regarding (Deuteronomy 7:10), "and He repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:93: Thus far have come the matters of contemplation that we found in the words of our sages, of blessed memory, and of the commentators, of blessed memory, which a person is obligated to examine in order to know the Creator's love, so that through this he be spurred on in his service and fulfill it out of love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:1: Since we have already, in the preceding chapters, discussed the things that arouse love, and said in the previous chapter that all the miracles performed for us were performed through the Shechinah, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is this how you repay the Lord?" — and on account of this we are obligated to arouse love for her — we thought it fitting to attach this chapter to it, to explain the several matters in which it is fitting for us to direct love specifically toward her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:2: It has already been made known that we are called sons, as it is said (ibid. 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God"; and it is known that it is the way of a son to strive for the honor of his mother, as explained in chapter 3, where our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Kiddushin 31a) that this is the reason it says (Exodus 20:12), "honor your father and your mother" — for a son's way is to honor his mother even more, and therefore Scripture placed the father first in the command of honor — and this surely stems from love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:3: The difference between a servant and a son is that a servant sometimes serves in order to receive reward, but a son does not serve in order to receive reward, but rather out of love for his father and mother — and so it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Kedoshim 82a). And there is a son whose soul is from Atzilut, and they say there (83a) that a son who is from there does not engage in Torah in order to receive reward, neither in deed, nor in speech, nor in thought. — end of quotation. And likewise, one whose soul is from there does not commit sin (ibid.).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:4: Although we find Israel also called "servants," as it is said (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me, they are My servants," it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Pinchas 223a) that from the side of the Shechinah they are called servants, because she is the one who serves her husband, in these words: the three patriarchs are called servants from the side of the Shechinah, which is the service [avodah] of the Lord — and so also Moses is called "servant of the Lord" — and therefore, "for the children of Israel are servants to Me" [from her side]; but with regard to others, all Israel are sons of kings, from the side of Malchut. And why is she called "service"? Because it is the way of a wife to serve her husband, and the way of sons to serve their father. — end of quotation. The intent of this, as we explained above, is that the Shechinah always arouses song, as it says (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not be silent, do not hold Your peace" — and she requires, for her own arousal, the arousal of the deeds of Israel who cling to her; and in this respect they are called servants.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:5: Whoever wishes to cling to the love of the Shechinah must always arouse deeds toward her — Torah or a commandment — in order to arouse toward her the "female waters" [mayin nukvin, arousal from below]. The proof is from Benjamin, whom the Zohar explains, parashat Vayetze (153b), is a chariot to the Shechinah in the secret of the female waters — for he leaped into the sea, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Sotah, ch. 5, 37a) on the verse (Psalms 68:28), "there Benjamin, the youngest, ruling [rodem] them" — in these words: "there Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them" — Rabbi Meir would say: when Israel passed through the sea, the tribes were competing with one another, this one saying I will go down first, and that one saying I will go down first. The tribe of Benjamin leaped and went down into the sea first, as it is said, "there Benjamin, the youngest, rodem" — do not read "rodem" but "radim" [descending]. And the princes of Judah were stoning [rogmim] them, as it is said, "the princes of Judah, their stoning" [interpreted so]. Therefore Benjamin merited to become the host to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:12), "and between his shoulders He dwells." — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:6: The reason the tribes competed over who would enter first is that the splitting of the Sea of Reeds required an arousal from below — this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses (Exodus 14:15), "why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the children of Israel that they should journey [forward]" — meaning, that they should begin to enter the sea, this being an indication of their faith that it would split for them; and through this arousal, that they begin, the sea would split for them: "and you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it." And because the tribe of Benjamin knew the root of their father's soul, which is the source and root for arousal from below, they therefore began immediately, in that same eagerness, and leaped into the sea; therefore they merited that the Shechinah be in their portion — namely, the Temple, which was built in the portion of Benjamin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:7: We learn from this matter that whoever wishes the Holy One, blessed be He, to perform for him a miracle, which is a change of nature, must first change his own nature in service to Him — as with the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, which is a thing outside of nature. Therefore it says in the Zohar (parashat Beshalach 52b) that this depends upon Atika [the Ancient One], for from there "teva" [nature], which is "Elohim," changes and turns into mercy — and therefore the tribe of Benjamin needed to do something contrary to nature, to leap into the sea.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:8: We further learn from this that even the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, which depends on Atika, required an arousal from below — and Atika is unrestrained generosity and simple mercy — how much more so did an arousal from below have to be needed for things that depend on the lower attributes, in Ze'ir [Anpin], which is the place of judgment, and in the female [Nukva], which is the place of judgment in essence, called "Tzedek," a judgment with no generosity at all — surely there an arousal is always needed, and in her lies the essential place of arousal, as explained regarding Benjamin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:9: Further it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayechi 244b) that the Shechinah is not unified in the secret of the love of union except through the souls of the righteous, in these words: Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Song of Songs 8:6), "set me as a seal upon your heart," etc. — I have already been aroused by this verse, but one night, when I stood before my father, I heard from him a matter: that there is no completeness, desire, and longing of the Assembly of Israel for the Holy One, blessed be He, except through the souls of the righteous, for they arouse the flow of the lower waters toward the upper, and at that moment the completeness of desire in a single clinging occurs, to make fruit. — end of quotation. Since the matter depends on them, it is fitting to hasten to bind oneself in her love in order to arouse the supernal love, and through this they are bound to the Shechinah, as explained further there, that the Shechinah is found between two righteous men, and of this it is said, "the righteous shall inherit the land."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:10: Now, all this arousal depends on the deeds of the righteous, even at the time the Temple stood — as explained above in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1, that after the completion of the sacrificial offering, Israel would stand at their station and the Levites in their song and music, so that there was always an arousal ascending — how much more so now, in our many sins, in this great and bitter exile, when the Shechinah has no arousal from the sacrificial offering, only a small support through the deeds of the righteous, who must support her a little from her fall — she being the "fallen tabernacle of David," which falls further each day than the day before, and all this because of our sins, as it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away" — for through sins she falls, and through good deeds she is raised up and given support, as is explained in the Zohar (parashat Shemini 40a), in these words: Rabbi Yehudah opened and said (Song of Songs 2:5), "support me with raisin cakes, spread apples around me," etc. — this verse has already been explained well, but the Assembly of Israel says this in exile: "support me" — what is "support me"? Rather, one who has fallen needs support, this being what is written (Psalms 145:14), "the Lord supports all who fall," etc. Therefore the Assembly of Israel, having fallen — as it is written, "she has fallen, she shall no more rise" — needs support, and she says, "support me" — support whom? Israel, her children, who are with her in exile. And with what? "With raisin cakes" — these are the patriarchs, who were first filled with that good wine that is preserved; and whoever knows how to unify the Holy Name, even though blessings are not found in the world, supports and sustains the Assembly of Israel in exile. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:11: If so, according to this, since the Shechinah asks of Israel her children to support her — for her support surely depends upon us, namely through the unifications in our prayer and our Torah, which are a support and sustenance for her — even though there is no union in exile, we must support her through unification, for through this some illumination comes to her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:12: My master, may his rest be in Eden, used to say that this is like the parable of a king who was banished from his kingdom and went into exile — one who does him the kindness of giving him a loaf of bread and a jug of water, that small amount is as precious in the king's eyes as if he had fed him fattened chickens while he stood in his kingdom. Similar to this parable, it is said in the Tikkunim (146b), in these words: rather, certainly, when the Shechinah is in exile, whoever performs a commandment to raise her up from exile is as if he honored the Holy One, blessed be He. This is like a king who had a quarrel with the queen and cast her out of his palace, and she went to dwell with a commoner — is it not that whoever receives her into his house and honors her surely honors the king, and brings about peace between her and her husband? Is not all the honor done for her, done for the king? For if the king was angry with her once or twice, he will be reconciled with her and return her to his house, and he asks her, who honored you, or who disgraced you, or if he banished her to another kingdom in a similar manner. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject. The rest we shall quote further on, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:13: This is the Shechinah's desire, that we always unify her — whether in prayer, whether in the performance of a commandment such as acts of lovingkindness and other commandments, whether in the engagement with Torah — and all these aspects are explained in the Zohar and the Tikkunim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:14: Regarding prayer, it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayakhel 200a), on the verse (Exodus 35:5), "take from among yourselves an offering [terumah]" — that the terumah is the Shechinah together with her husband, who are two out of a hundred [i.e., trei mei-me'ah, an allusion in the word terumah], and it says: and when we need to raise up this lower female, it is forbidden for us to take her alone, but rather her and her husband, they being the two of the hundred we mentioned — for it is not necessary to separate them at all, but rather to unify her and her husband, and therefore it is called "terumah" as one complete term. And come and see: every day a herald proclaims, all people of the world, this matter stands upon you — "take from among yourselves an offering for the Lord" — and should you say this matter is difficult for you, "whoever is of a willing heart shall bring it." What is "shall bring it"? Rather, from here we learn the secret of a person's prayer, etc. And they explained there that all of prayer, with the hymns, with the blessings of the Shema and the Eighteen Benedictions, is entirely a rectification for the Shechinah, to unify her, and they elaborated at length there. And the whole reality of this unification depends on the intention of the heart — "whoever is of a willing heart shall bring it" — meaning, shall bring her up above and unify her; and so he says at the end of the passage: therefore happy is he who sets his heart and his will to this, and therefore it is written, "whoever is of a willing heart shall bring the offering of the Lord" — to the King; his heart shall bring [her] to the Supernal King, as has been said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:15: Regarding the commandments, it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Ki Tetze 281a), in these words: it is not for nothing that the Holy One, blessed be He, says: whoever engages in Torah and in acts of lovingkindness and prays with the congregation, I credit it to him as if he had redeemed Me and My children from among the nations — and yet how many people engage in Torah and perform acts of lovingkindness, and the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are not [thereby] redeemed! Rather, this refers to one who engages in Torah in order to unite it with the Holy One, blessed be He; and as for acts of lovingkindness, they have already established that "there is no chasid except one who deals kindly [mitchased] with his Creator" — for all the commandments one performs are to redeem His Shechinah through them, and thereby one performs kindness with the Holy One, blessed be He. Whoever performs kindness with the Holy One, blessed be He, performs it with His Shechinah — for when Israel sinned and the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to discipline them, the Mother [Shechinah] would lie prostrate over them until they went to evil ways; what did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He drove out the King's son and the Queen, and He swore that He would not return to His place until the Queen returned to her place. And whoever returns in repentance and performs kindness for the Shechinah, and for the whole Torah and its commandments — and it [the Torah] is only for redeeming the Shechinah — this one performs kindness with his Creator, and it is as though he has redeemed her, and His Shechinah, and His children.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:16: Elijah and all the heads of the academies said: Faithful Shepherd, you are that man — you are, besides the King and the Queen, the one whose efforts toward the Holy One, blessed be He, are not like one who performs kindness with his Creator, but like a son who obligates himself to place his own being and strength to redeem father and mother, giving himself over to death for them — for whoever is not the King's son and does good for the King and the Queen, this is certainly considered as one who performs kindness with his Creator [i.e., as an ordinary act of piety, not as filial devotion].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:17: The Faithful Shepherd rose and prostrated himself before the Holy One, blessed be He, and wept, and said: so may it be His will, that He consider me as a son, that my deeds toward the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah be to Him like a man who exerts himself for his father and mother, whom he loves more than himself, his soul, his spirit, and his neshamah, and his entire world that he possesses he considers as nothing, to do the will of father and mother and to redeem them through it. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:18: As for what is said, that all the commandments one performs are to redeem the Shechinah through them — the intent of this redemption is her unification, for through her unification she ascends from the exile, which is the kelipot, and she is purified, refined, and unified with her husband.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:19: As for what is said, "and thereby one performs kindness with the Holy One, blessed be He" — this is because the King without the Queen is not [fully] a king, and His completeness is with her completeness. And so it is said in the Tikkunim (146b), in these words, in brief: in this manner, the Holy One, blessed be He, drove out the Shechinah and cast her from His house — this is what is written (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away" — and is it not that whoever honors her in exile honors the Holy One, blessed be He, or whoever disgraces her disgraces the Holy One, blessed be He? Therefore, "those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed." — end of quotation. And he said above this, that the honor of the Shechinah is to perform the commandment to raise her from exile, in these words: when the Shechinah is in exile, whoever performs a commandment to raise her from exile is as if he honored the Holy One, blessed be He. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:20: Without doubt, performing the commandment with fear and love thereby gives her ascent and removal from the exile, which is the kelipot, as it says in the Tikkunim (25b): a commandment without fear and love cannot ascend and stand before the Lord. It follows that the wings that lift her upward, so that the kelipot cannot grasp her, are fear and love — and without them she cannot ascend. Regarding the matter of engaging in the commandments, we shall elaborate on this further, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:21: Regarding "who is a chasid? One who deals kindly with his Creator," it is further explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Pinchas 222b) that the Torah was given from the right side, which is Chesed, and one who engages in Torah for the sake of unification is called a chasid, one who deals kindly with his Creator, in these words: the Torah was given from the right side of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is Chesed; therefore whoever engages in Torah is called a chasid — therefore I say to the Holy One, blessed be He, "guard my soul, for I am a chasid" — and do not judge her like the deeds of these ignorant common people, of whom it is said, "an ignorant person cannot be a chasid." And should you say, how many common people there are who perform kindness — rather, they have thus established: who is a chasid? One who deals kindly with his Creator — such as David, who would join [things] together — and what would he join? The supernal Torah he would join with the Holy One, blessed be He; therefore, "guard my soul, for I am a chasid." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:22: And in the Tikkunim (end of p. 1), they further explained regarding this, in these words: the chasidim are from the side of Chesed, the grade of Abraham, and they have established regarding him, "there is no chasid except one who deals kindly with his Creator" — for he makes for Him a nest [ken], which is His lodging, and this is the Shechinah, which is His nest, His house. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:23: It seems to me that these words may be understood together with what is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Ki Tetze 276b), in these words: he opened and said, Faithful Shepherd, this bride of yours, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave her to Abraham to raise her for Us [or: for you]; and because he guarded her, she is called his daughter — this is what is written, "he had a daughter... and her name was..." and by her he fulfilled the whole Torah, even the joining of cooked dishes [eruv tavshilin] — this is what is written (Genesis 26:5), "and he kept My charge," etc. — and he was to her like a foster-father, as (Esther 2:7), "and he was foster-father to Hadassah" — and the Holy One, blessed be He, blessed him for her sake, this being what is written (Genesis 24:1), "and the Lord blessed Abraham in all things" — and he raised her with all good attributes, and dealt kindness with her, and raised her in greatness with the attribute of Chesed of Abraham, and his house was open wide for her sake, to perform kindness with all who come into the world. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:24: We find ourselves taught by this passage that the essential act of lovingkindness that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, performed was to deal kindness with the Shechinah, and this in two respects: first, that she be complete with all the good attributes, and second, to bind her to Chesed, and his house was open wide to perform kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:25: The explanation that she be complete with all good attributes is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 159b), where it says that the Shechinah, all six weekdays, goes wandering from place to place to see whether she can find a righteous man to whom she may cling; and it says afterward, and who is the righteous man to whom she clings, that he be a chariot for the Righteous One, Life of the worlds — one who is complete with all good attributes — and it says, in these words: and who is the righteous man to whom she clings? That one who is complete with all the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is said "and they were completed" [vaychulu] — complete with everything, in whom all the sefirot are included — one who is a chasid and performs kindness with the Shechinah, and gives her strength through Gevurah, and so with every single sefirah, giving her strength through it — and through him she clings and does not move from him throughout all six days of the week, and for his sake it is said, "the world stands upon one righteous man" — and through him "the wings of the dove are covered with silver" (Psalms 68:14) — she covers herself over him with her wings and shields him from all the accusers of the world. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:26: Here it is explicitly said that one must be complete with all the good attributes among the ten sefirot, so that the Shechinah receives from him strength and illumination from each and every attribute, for she receives only through the righteous man, and therefore they must be complete in him — this is what is said, "and so with every single sefirah, giving her strength through it." And although here he explained only "performs kindness" and "mighty," he relies on what is explained regarding the ten attributes in the Tikkunim elsewhere, and we shall explain them further on, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:27: Regarding engaging in Torah to unify the Shechinah, it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 97b), in these words: meanwhile, the Faithful Shepherd comes, taking a sling-stone in his hand; he opened and said: "Zarka Makef Shofar Holech Segolta" [the names of cantillation notes], taking three stones and casting them upward; and when he casts them, they become a single stone, and he says to the Masters of the Academies: receive this stone among you, for the Shechinah is in exile and there is none among you to arouse toward her, to appease her toward her husband. Not only that, but how many masters of study-halls, colleagues among you, cry out every day and every night with the Oral Torah, with several difficulties, crying out over it like dogs, saying "give, give," like Gehinnom, which cries out "give, give" — this is what is written (Proverbs 30:15), "the leech has two daughters: give, give" — give us wealth in this world, give us wealth in the World to Come — as they have established (end of Avot ch. 2), "study much Torah and you shall be given much reward" — and there is none who engages in Torah to raise up through it the Shechinah from exile and to unite her with her husband, for their eyes are sealed and their hearts closed.
